n.az: hazırlayan şəxs və ya şirkət, proqramçı

expressions.usage: Business: design and create something for sale
relationship = the way people are connected
software is uncountable: "a software" is wrong
Academic; theory = a set of ideas that explains something
system = an organised way of doing something
technology = scientific knowledge used in practice
method = a planned way of doing something

sentences.en: The company is developing a new product.
sentences.az: Şirkət yeni məhsul hazırlayır.

sentences.en: Scientists have developed a new method of treating the disease.
sentences.az: Alimlər xəstəliyin müalicəsi üçün yeni üsul işləyib hazırlayıblar.

sentences.en: The child is developing normally.
sentences.az: Uşaq normal inkişaf edir.

sentences.en: Travelling is good for your personal development.
sentences.az: Səyahət etmək şəxsi inkişafınız üçün faydalıdır.

usage: DEVELOP has no final "e": develop, developed, developing, development. Like IMPROVE it is both transitive (develop a product) and intransitive (The town developed quickly). "A developing country" is still building its economy; "a developed country" already has a strong one. With illnesses it means "begin to have": develop a cough.

lessons.azerbaijani: təcrübə; başa gələn hadisə, təəssürat; yaşamaq, üzləşmək

expressions.usage: practical = connected with real situations, not theory
valuable = very useful or worth a lot
Introduces an opinion based on what you have seen

sentences.en: She gained a lot of experience working abroad.
sentences.az: O, xaricdə işləyərkən çoxlu təcrübə qazandı.

sentences.en: Do you have any previous experience of this type of work?
sentences.az: Bu növ iş üzrə əvvəlki təcrübəniz varmı?

sentences.en: Visiting Shusha was an unforgettable experience.
sentences.az: Şuşaya səfər unudulmaz təəssürat idi.

sentences.en: In my experience, children learn faster than adults.
sentences.az: Mənim təcrübəmə görə, uşaqlar böyüklərdən daha tez öyrənirlər.

usage: EXPERIENCE is uncountable when it means knowledge or skill from doing something ("He has a lot of experience" – no plural), and countable when it means an event that affected you ("an unforgettable experience"). Azerbaijani "təcrübə" also means a scientific test, but that is EXPERIMENT in English. As a verb it is rather formal: "experience difficulties".

expressions.usage: technical = connected with the practical use of machines or methods
presentation = a talk that gives information

sentences.en: Good communication skills are essential for this job.
sentences.az: Bu iş üçün yaxşı ünsiyyət bacarıqları zəruridir.

sentences.en: This work requires a lot of skill.
sentences.az: Bu iş böyük məharət tələb edir.

sentences.en: It takes years to master a skill.
sentences.az: Bir bacarığa mükəmməl yiyələnmək illər çəkir.

sentences.en: The course will help you improve your presentation skills.
sentences.az: Kurs təqdimat bacarıqlarınızı yaxşılaşdırmağa kömək edəcək.

usage: SKILL is countable for particular abilities ("computer skills", "a useful skill") and uncountable for ability in general ("a task that requires skill"). SKILLED describes trained workers or work (skilled workers); SKILFUL describes how well someone does something (a skilful player). American spelling: skillful. Use AT or IN: "skilled at negotiating", "skill in dealing with people".

lessons.azerbaijani: idarə etmək, rəhbərlik etmək; bacarmaq, öhdəsindən gəlmək

adj.az: idarə oluna bilən, öhdəsindən gəlmək mümkün olan

expressions.az: nəyisə bacarmaq, bir işin öhdəsindən gəlmək
expressions.usage: Success in something difficult; always with "to"
project = a planned piece of work
budget = a plan for spending money
staff = all the workers of an organisation
department = a section of a company or university
on your own = alone, without help

sentences.en: I managed to finish the report on time.
sentences.az: Hesabatı vaxtında bitirə bildim.

sentences.en: She manages a team of twenty people.
sentences.az: O, iyirmi nəfərlik komandaya rəhbərlik edir.

sentences.en: Can you manage on your own?
sentences.az: Təkbaşına bacararsan?

sentences.en: Exercise helps me manage stress.
sentences.az: İdman mənə stressin öhdəsindən gəlməyə kömək edir.

usage: MANAGE has two main meanings. 1) To control or be in charge of a business, people or resources: manage a department. 2) To succeed in doing something difficult: MANAGE TO + infinitive. For one successful action in the past, use "managed to", not "could": "I managed to open the door". "Can you manage?" is a polite offer of help.

expressions.usage: report = a written or spoken description of a situation
Intransitive + FOR; interview = a formal meeting with questions
Often for bad news: Prepare yourself for a shock
be prepared to + infinitive = be willing to
With food, "prepare" is more formal than "make"
summary = a short statement of the main points
essay = a short piece of writing on one subject

sentences.en: I have to prepare a report for tomorrow's meeting.
sentences.az: Sabahkı iclas üçün hesabat hazırlamalıyam.

sentences.en: How did you prepare for the interview?
sentences.az: Müsahibəyə necə hazırlaşdın?

sentences.en: Hope for the best, but prepare for the worst.
sentences.az: Ən yaxşısına ümid et, amma ən pisinə hazır ol.

sentences.en: I am not prepared to wait any longer.
sentences.az: Mən daha gözləməyə hazır deyiləm.

usage: PREPARE + object means to make something ready (prepare a report); PREPARE FOR + noun means to get yourself ready (prepare for an exam). "Be prepared to do something" usually means to be willing, not just ready: "Are you prepared to work at weekends?" The noun PREPARATION is uncountable in general (exam preparation) and plural for practical arrangements (wedding preparations).

lessons.azerbaijani: işə götürmək, işlə təmin etmək; (üsul) tətbiq etmək

expressions.usage: full-time = for all the normal working hours
part-time = for only part of the working week
agency = a business that provides a service
youth = young people as a group
rate = a measurement of how often something happens
temporary = lasting for a limited time
permanent = lasting for a long time or for ever

sentences.en: The factory employs over five hundred people.
sentences.az: Zavodda beş yüzdən çox adam çalışır.

sentences.en: He is looking for full-time employment.
sentences.az: O, tam ştatlı iş axtarır.

sentences.en: Youth unemployment is a serious problem in many countries.
sentences.az: Gənclər arasında işsizlik bir çox ölkədə ciddi problemdir.

sentences.en: The unemployment rate fell to five per cent.
sentences.az: İşsizlik səviyyəsi beş faizə düşdü.

usage: EMPLOY is more formal than "give a job to" or "take on". Note the pair EMPLOYER (the company or person who pays) and EMPLOYEE (the person who works). EMPLOYMENT and UNEMPLOYMENT are uncountable. "Unemployed" describes people; "the unemployed" means unemployed people as a group. In formal writing EMPLOY also means "use": employ a method.

lessons.azerbaijani: müraciət etmək, ərizə vermək; tətbiq etmək; aid olmaq

n.az: ərizə, müraciət, həmçinin tətbiq və proqram (app)

expressions.usage: apply FOR + the thing you want
loan = money that you borrow from a bank
scholarship = money given to a student to pay for study
form = an official document with spaces to fill in
British spelling of the noun: licence

sentences.en: I have applied for a visa to study in the UK.
sentences.az: Mən Böyük Britaniyada təhsil almaq üçün vizaya müraciət etmişəm.

sentences.en: Please fill in the application form.
sentences.az: Zəhmət olmasa, ərizə formasını doldurun.

sentences.en: She applied for a scholarship and got it.
sentences.az: O, təqaüd üçün müraciət etdi və onu qazandı.

sentences.en: Students should apply their knowledge to real problems.
sentences.az: Tələbələr biliklərini real problemlərə tətbiq etməlidirlər.

usage: APPLY has three patterns. 1) apply FOR something you want (a job, a visa) and apply TO an organisation (apply to a university). 2) apply something TO something = use it in practice (apply a rule, apply knowledge). 3) apply TO somebody = be relevant ("This rule applies to everyone"). APPLICATION means both the request and the computer program; APPLICANT is the person who applies.

expressions.usage: primary = first; for children of about 5 to 11
secondary = for pupils of about 11 to 18
private = paid for by parents, not by the state
training = learning the skills for a job
access TO = the right or chance to use something

sentences.en: Higher education is free in some countries.
sentences.az: Bəzi ölkələrdə ali təhsil pulsuzdur.

sentences.en: Every child has the right to receive an education.
sentences.az: Hər bir uşağın təhsil almaq hüququ var.

sentences.en: Many girls in the world still have no access to education.
sentences.az: Dünyada bir çox qızın hələ də təhsil almaq imkanı yoxdur.

sentences.en: The government spends a lot of money on education and training.
sentences.az: Hökumət təhsilə və peşə hazırlığına çoxlu pul xərcləyir.

usage: EDUCATION is usually uncountable (the education system), but it takes "an" when you describe one person's schooling: "a good education", "receive an education". EDUCATIONAL describes things that teach (an educational programme); EDUCATED describes people (a well-educated woman). Do not confuse it with UPBRINGING (tərbiyə), which is the way parents bring up a child.

expressions.usage: explain + wh-clause: explain why / how / what
purpose = the reason for doing something

sentences.en: Can you explain why you were late?
sentences.az: Niyə gecikdiyini izah edə bilərsən?

sentences.en: The teacher explained the rule to us.
sentences.az: Müəllim qaydanı bizə izah etdi.

sentences.en: There must be a logical explanation for this.
sentences.az: Bunun məntiqi bir izahı olmalıdır.

sentences.en: Let me briefly explain the purpose of this meeting.
sentences.az: İcazə verin, bu iclasın məqsədini qısaca izah edim.

usage: The person comes after TO: "explain something TO somebody". "Explain me the rule" is a very common mistake; say "Explain the rule to me". EXPLAIN is often followed by a clause: explain that / why / how. The noun EXPLANATION drops the "i" of the verb (explain – explanation) and takes FOR or OF: "an explanation for the delay".

lessons.azerbaijani: təklif etmək, fikir irəli sürmək; nəyəsə işarə etmək

expressions.usage: suggest (that) + clause: I suggest (that) we wait
Fixed phrase: at my / her suggestion
activity = something you do for interest or pleasure

sentences.en: I suggest that we take a short break.
sentences.az: Təklif edirəm ki, qısa fasilə edək.

sentences.en: He suggested going by train.
sentences.az: O, qatarla getməyi təklif etdi.

sentences.en: Can anyone suggest an alternative?
sentences.az: Kimsə başqa variant təklif edə bilərmi?

sentences.en: We welcome suggestions from our customers.
sentences.az: Biz müştərilərimizin təkliflərini məmnuniyyətlə qarşılayırıq.

usage: SUGGEST is never followed by "to + infinitive" or by a person as direct object. Correct patterns: suggest + -ing (He suggested going), suggest + that-clause (He suggested that we go), suggest + noun (suggest a plan), suggest something TO somebody. Wrong: "He suggested me to go". In academic writing SUGGEST also means "indicate": "The results suggest that ...". OFFER is used when you are willing to give or do something yourself.

lessons.azerbaijani: mübahisə etmək, höcətləşmək; iddia etmək, əsaslandırmaq

expressions.usage: argue WITH a person ABOUT / OVER a subject

expressions.az: nəyinsə belə olduğunu iddia etmək, əsaslandırmaq
expressions.usage: Academic use: give reasons for an opinion

expressions.az: əleyhinə çıxış etmək, qarşı dəlil gətirmək
expressions.usage: Opposite: argue for / in favour of
convincing = making you believe that something is true

sentences.en: My brothers are always arguing with each other.
sentences.az: Qardaşlarım həmişə bir-biri ilə mübahisə edirlər.

sentences.en: Some experts argue that the law should be changed.
sentences.az: Bəzi mütəxəssislər qanunun dəyişdirilməli olduğunu iddia edirlər.

sentences.en: We had an argument about money.
sentences.az: Biz pul üstündə mübahisə etdik.

sentences.en: That is not a very convincing argument.
sentences.az: Bu, o qədər də inandırıcı dəlil deyil.

usage: ARGUE has two quite different uses. In everyday speech it means to disagree angrily: argue WITH somebody ABOUT something. In essays and academic texts it means to give reasons for an opinion: "The author argues that ...". The noun ARGUMENT has both meanings too: a quarrel, or a reason supporting an idea. Spelling: the "e" is dropped in ARGUMENT.

expressions.usage: complain ABOUT + the problem; delay = a period of waiting
complain OF + a pain or illness
customer = a person who buys goods or services
A polite way to say you are satisfied

sentences.en: Several passengers complained about the delay.
sentences.az: Bir neçə sərnişin gecikmədən şikayət etdi.

sentences.en: She went to the doctor complaining of a headache.
sentences.az: O, baş ağrısından şikayət edərək həkimə getdi.

sentences.en: I would like to make a formal complaint.
sentences.az: Mən rəsmi şikayət etmək istəyirəm.

sentences.en: How's work? – Can't complain.
sentences.az: İş necədir? – Pis deyil.

usage: COMPLAIN is the verb and COMPLAINT (with a final "t") the noun. Patterns: complain TO a person ABOUT a problem; complain OF a pain or symptom; complain THAT + clause. You "make" a complaint (not "do"). In British service situations people often begin politely: "I'm afraid I have a complaint about ...".

expressions.usage: matter = a subject or situation that must be dealt with
group = a number of people together
Fixed phrase: the plan under discussion
lively = full of energy and interest
politics = the ideas and activities of government
colleague = a person you work with
advantage = something that helps; opposite: disadvantage

sentences.en: We need to discuss the matter with the manager.
sentences.az: Bu məsələni müdirlə müzakirə etməliyik.

sentences.en: I never discuss politics at work.
sentences.az: Mən işdə heç vaxt siyasətdən danışmıram.

sentences.en: There was a lively discussion after the lecture.
sentences.az: Mühazirədən sonra canlı müzakirə oldu.

sentences.en: The essay should discuss the advantages and disadvantages of online learning.
sentences.az: Essedə onlayn təhsilin üstünlükləri və mənfi cəhətləri müzakirə olunmalıdır.

usage: DISCUSS takes a direct object with no preposition: "discuss a problem", never "discuss about a problem". (The noun does take one: "a discussion about / of the problem".) You discuss something WITH somebody. In exam essay questions, "Discuss" means: write about the different sides of the subject and give your opinion.

expressions.usage: The standard way to give your view; not "according to me"
poll = asking many people the same question
honest = saying what is true; the "h" is silent
expert = a person with special knowledge
popular = of ordinary people; liked by many

sentences.en: In my opinion, this is the best solution.
sentences.az: Mənim fikrimcə, bu, ən yaxşı həll yoludur.

sentences.en: Everyone has the right to express an opinion.
sentences.az: Hər kəsin fikir bildirmək hüququ var.

sentences.en: I'd like your honest opinion about my essay.
sentences.az: Essem haqqında səmimi fikrini bilmək istərdim.

sentences.en: If you are not sure, ask for a second opinion.
sentences.az: Əmin deyilsənsə, ikinci rəy al.

usage: To give your view, say "In my opinion, ..." or "I think ...", not "According to me" and not "In my opinion, I think" (this repeats the idea). The prepositions are OF, ABOUT and ON: "What is your opinion of the film?", "opinions on education". Useful verbs: have / hold / express / give an opinion. In IELTS essays, vary it with "in my view" and "from my point of view".

expressions.usage: The way to count it: one piece of advice, two pieces of advice
offer = say that you are willing to give

sentences.en: Let me give you a piece of advice.
sentences.az: İcazə ver, sənə bir məsləhət verim.

sentences.en: You should seek medical advice if the pain continues.
sentences.az: Ağrı davam edərsə, həkimə müraciət etməlisiniz.

sentences.en: The doctor advised me to rest for a few days.
sentences.az: Həkim mənə bir neçə gün dincəlməyi məsləhət gördü.

sentences.en: He ignored my advice and lost all his money.
sentences.az: O, məsləhətimə məhəl qoymadı və bütün pulunu itirdi.

usage: ADVICE (/ədˈvaɪs/, noun, with "c") is uncountable: no "an advice", no "advices". Say "some advice" or "a piece of advice". ADVISE (/ədˈvaɪz/, verb, with "s") follows the pattern advise + person + to-infinitive, or advise + -ing: "I advise waiting". The same c/s difference appears in practice / practise. Verbs used with the noun: give, offer, ask for, seek, take, follow, ignore.

expressions.usage: agree WITH a person or an opinion
agree TO + infinitive = say yes to a request
sign = write your name on a document
trade = buying and selling between countries
Idiomatic: "I couldn't agree more" = I agree completely
Agree with the general idea, not yet with the details
tend to = usually do; it softens the statement

sentences.en: I agree with you.
sentences.az: Mən səninlə razıyam.

sentences.en: She agreed to help us.
sentences.az: O bizə kömək etməyə razılıq verdi.

sentences.en: The two countries signed a trade agreement.
sentences.az: İki ölkə ticarət sazişi imzaladı.

sentences.en: I couldn't agree more.
sentences.az: Tamamilə razıyam.

usage: AGREE is a verb, so say "I agree", never "I am agree". Prepositions change the meaning: agree WITH a person or opinion; agree TO a proposal or to do something; agree ON / ABOUT a subject you decide together ("We agreed on a price"). It is not normally used in continuous tenses. To disagree politely: "I'm afraid I don't agree" or "I see your point, but ...".

expressions.usage: decide ON + noun = choose after thinking
decide whether / what / where + clause or to-infinitive
regret = feel sorry about something you did
moment = a very short period of time

sentences.en: We decided to stay at home.
sentences.az: Biz evdə qalmağı qərara aldıq.

sentences.en: Have you decided on a name for the baby?
sentences.az: Körpə üçün ad seçmisiniz?

sentences.en: I can't decide whether to accept the job.
sentences.az: İşi qəbul edib-etməməyə qərar verə bilmirəm.

sentences.en: It was a tough decision, but I don't regret it.
sentences.az: Bu, çətin qərar idi, amma peşman deyiləm.

usage: DECIDE + to-infinitive is the basic pattern: "I decided to leave" (not "decided leaving"). DECIDE ON + noun means to choose one thing: "decide on a date". The noun DECISION collocates with MAKE in general English ("make a decision"); British English also uses "take a decision", especially for official ones. A DECISIVE person decides quickly; a decisive moment or victory settles the result.

expressions.usage: pollution = damage to air, water or land by harmful substances

expressions.az: ekoloji şüur, ətraf mühit haqqında maariflilik
expressions.usage: awareness = knowing that something exists and is important
preserve = keep in its original state
stable = not likely to change; here "environment" = conditions
disaster = an event causing great damage
destroy = damage so badly that it no longer exists

sentences.en: We must do more to preserve the environment.
sentences.az: Ətraf mühiti qoruyub saxlamaq üçün daha çox iş görməliyik.

sentences.en: Environmental pollution is a danger to our health.
sentences.az: Ətraf mühitin çirklənməsi sağlamlığımız üçün təhlükədir.

sentences.en: The oil spill was an environmental disaster.
sentences.az: Neft dağılması ekoloji fəlakət idi.

sentences.en: Children need a stable environment at home.
sentences.az: Uşaqların evdə sabit mühitə ehtiyacı var.

usage: With "the", THE ENVIRONMENT means the natural world: air, water, land, plants and animals. With "a/an" and an adjective it means the conditions around a person: a working environment, a learning environment. Watch the spelling: enviroNment. "Environmentally friendly" describes products that do not harm nature. This word family is essential for IELTS Writing Task 2.

expressions.usage: wildlife = animals and plants living in natural conditions
skin = the outer covering of the body
forest = a large area of trees
rights = things the law allows you to have or do
data = information, especially stored on computers
glove = a covering for the hand

sentences.en: Sun cream protects your skin against the sun.
sentences.az: Günəş kremi dərinizi günəşdən qoruyur.

sentences.en: New laws are needed to protect wildlife.
sentences.az: Vəhşi təbiəti qorumaq üçün yeni qanunlar lazımdır.

sentences.en: Workers must wear protective gloves.
sentences.az: İşçilər qoruyucu əlcək geyinməlidirlər.

sentences.en: What can each of us do to protect the planet?
sentences.az: Planeti qorumaq üçün hər birimiz nə edə bilərik?

usage: PROTECT is used with FROM or AGAINST: "protect children from harm", "protect the skin against the sun". PROTECT means to keep safe from possible harm; DEFEND means to act against an attack that is happening; GUARD means to watch a place or person; PRESERVE means to keep something as it is. The adjective PROTECTIVE describes both equipment (protective clothing) and caring behaviour (protective parents).

expressions.usage: sales = the number of items sold
risk = the possibility of something bad happening
steady = continuing gradually without sudden changes
increase BY + the size of the change; per cent = %
production = the process of making goods
income = money that you earn or receive

sentences.en: Prices have increased by ten per cent this year.
sentences.az: Bu il qiymətlər on faiz artıb.

sentences.en: Smoking increases the risk of heart disease.
sentences.az: Siqaret çəkmək ürək xəstəliyi riskini artırır.

sentences.en: There has been a sharp increase in the number of tourists.
sentences.az: Turistlərin sayında kəskin artım olub.

sentences.en: The company plans to increase production next year.
sentences.az: Şirkət gələn il istehsalı artırmağı planlaşdırır.

usage: The stress moves: the verb is inCREASE, the noun is INcrease. The verb is both transitive (increase prices) and intransitive (Prices increased). Prepositions: an increase IN something (not "of"), increase BY 10 per cent (the difference), increase TO 50 (the final figure). This is core language for IELTS Writing Task 1; the opposite is DECREASE. INCREASINGLY means "more and more": increasingly popular.

expressions.usage: waste = unwanted material; using more than is needed
emissions = gases sent into the air
poverty = the state of being poor
reduce BY + amount; half = 50 per cent
traffic = the vehicles on the roads

sentences.en: We need to reduce the amount of plastic waste.
sentences.az: Plastik tullantıların miqdarını azaltmalıyıq.

sentences.en: Please reduce your speed near the school.
sentences.az: Zəhmət olmasa, məktəbin yaxınlığında sürəti azaldın.

sentences.en: The new road will reduce traffic in the city centre.
sentences.az: Yeni yol şəhərin mərkəzində nəqliyyat sıxlığını azaldacaq.

sentences.en: The government promised to reduce poverty.
sentences.az: Hökumət yoxsulluğu azaltmağa söz verdi.

usage: REDUCE is normally transitive: somebody reduces something. When nothing causes the change, use an intransitive verb such as FALL, DROP or DECREASE: "Prices fell" (not "Prices reduced"). Patterns: reduce something BY 20 per cent; reduce something FROM 100 TO 80. The noun REDUCTION takes IN: "a reduction in crime". In shops, "reduced" means cheaper than before.

expressions.usage: shelter = a place giving protection from weather or danger
provide FOR a family = give them what they need to live
feedback = comments on how good something is; uncountable
facilities = buildings, services or equipment for a purpose
security = protection against danger or crime
proof = facts showing that something is true

sentences.en: The organisation provides shelter for homeless people.
sentences.az: Təşkilat evsiz insanlara sığınacaq verir.

sentences.en: He works hard to provide for his family.
sentences.az: O, ailəsini dolandırmaq üçün çox işləyir.

sentences.en: You can borrow the car, provided that you bring it back today.
sentences.az: Maşını götürə bilərsən, bir şərtlə ki, bu gün qaytarasan.

sentences.en: Teachers should provide feedback on students' work.
sentences.az: Müəllimlər tələbələrin işləri haqqında rəy bildirməlidirlər.

usage: Two patterns with the same meaning: provide somebody WITH something ("The school provides students with books") and provide something FOR somebody ("The school provides books for students"). Not: "provide students books". PROVIDE is more formal than GIVE and is typical of reports and essays. PROVIDED THAT introduces a condition and is slightly more formal than "if".

expressions.usage: claim = a statement that something is true
moral = giving encouragement rather than practical help
charity = an organisation that helps people in need
Fixed phrase: speak in support of a plan
government = the group of people who rule a country

sentences.en: My parents gave me a lot of emotional support.
sentences.az: Valideynlərim mənə böyük mənəvi dəstək oldular.

sentences.en: Many students need financial support.
sentences.az: Bir çox tələbənin maliyyə dəstəyinə ehtiyacı var.

sentences.en: There is no evidence to support this claim.
sentences.az: Bu iddianı təsdiqləyən heç bir sübut yoxdur.

sentences.en: Which team do you support?
sentences.az: Sən hansı komandanın azarkeşisən?

usage: SUPPORT covers several Azerbaijani verbs: dəstəkləmək (support a plan), azarkeşlik etmək (support a team, British English), dolandırmaq (support a family) and əsaslandırmaq (support an argument with facts). The noun is uncountable: "a lot of support", not "a support". In essays, "support your opinion with examples" is a key instruction. SUPPORTIVE describes people who give help and encouragement.

expressions.usage: puzzle = a game or problem that tests your thinking
mystery = something that is difficult to explain
crisis = a time of great difficulty; plural: crises
effective = producing the result that is wanted
conflict = a serious disagreement or fight
obvious = easy to see or understand

sentences.en: Nobody has been able to solve the mystery.
sentences.az: Heç kim bu sirri aça bilməyib.

sentences.en: We need to find an effective solution to this problem.
sentences.az: Bu problemin səmərəli həll yolunu tapmalıyıq.

sentences.en: Both sides want a peaceful solution to the conflict.
sentences.az: Hər iki tərəf münaqişənin sülh yolu ilə həllini istəyir.

sentences.en: There is no obvious solution.
sentences.az: Göz qabağında olan bir həll yolu yoxdur.

usage: You SOLVE a problem, a puzzle, a mystery or a crime, but you ANSWER a question and you RESOLVE a dispute (resolve is more formal). The noun SOLUTION takes TO: "a solution TO the problem" (not "of"). Common verbs with solution: find, offer, propose, come up with. In chemistry, a SOLUTION is a liquid in which something is dissolved.

expressions.usage: accident = a sudden event causing damage or injury
crowd = a large number of people together
alcohol = drinks such as beer and wine

sentences.en: You should avoid eating late at night.
sentences.az: Gecə gec yemək yeməkdən çəkinməlisən.

sentences.en: The driver braked to avoid an accident.
sentences.az: Sürücü qəzadan yayınmaq üçün əyləci basdı.

sentences.en: We left early to avoid the crowds.
sentences.az: İzdihamdan uzaq olmaq üçün tez çıxdıq.

sentences.en: To avoid confusion, please write clearly.
sentences.az: Anlaşılmazlıq olmasın deyə, zəhmət olmasa, aydın yazın.

usage: AVOID is followed by a noun or by the -ing form: "avoid sugar", "avoid making mistakes". The infinitive is wrong: not "avoid to make". AVOID means to keep away from something; PREVENT means to stop something from happening at all (prevent an accident, prevent somebody from doing something). UNAVOIDABLE describes things that cannot be prevented: an unavoidable delay.

expressions.usage: pain = the feeling when part of your body hurts
effect = a change produced by a cause
root = the origin of a problem
disease = an illness with a specific name
injury = physical harm to the body

sentences.en: The heavy snow caused chaos on the roads.
sentences.az: Güclü qar yollarda xaos yaratdı.

sentences.en: The news caused great concern among parents.
sentences.az: Bu xəbər valideynlər arasında böyük narahatlıq doğurdu.

sentences.en: Police are still trying to find the cause of the fire.
sentences.az: Polis hələ də yanğının səbəbini araşdırır.

sentences.en: Poverty is the root cause of many social problems.
sentences.az: Yoxsulluq bir çox sosial problemin kök səbəbidir.

usage: As a verb, CAUSE usually has a negative object: cause damage, problems, pain, an accident. For good results, use "bring about", "lead to" or "result in". Patterns: cause something; cause somebody something ("cause him pain"); cause somebody TO do something. As a noun, note the prepositions: the cause OF a problem, but a reason FOR something. CAUSE is what makes something happen; REASON is the explanation given.

expressions.usage: worth = having value; be worth + noun / -ing
joint = done by two or more people together
determined = having decided firmly to succeed

expressions.az: bir məqsədlə, nəyəsə nail olmağa çalışaraq
expressions.usage: Formal linker: in an effort to + infinitive
desperate = ready to do anything because the situation is so bad
rescue = saving people from danger; plural "efforts" = organised activity

sentences.en: Learning a language takes time and effort.
sentences.az: Dil öyrənmək vaxt və zəhmət tələb edir.

sentences.en: It was hard work, but it was worth the effort.
sentences.az: Çətin iş idi, amma zəhmətinə dəyərdi.

sentences.en: The project was a joint effort between two universities.
sentences.az: Layihə iki universitetin birgə səyi idi.

sentences.en: The company cut prices in an effort to increase sales.
sentences.az: Şirkət satışları artırmaq məqsədi ilə qiymətləri endirdi.

usage: The basic collocation is MAKE an effort (not "do"): "make an effort to arrive on time". EFFORT is uncountable when it means energy in general (It takes effort) and countable for a particular attempt (a determined effort). The plural EFFORTS often means organised work: rescue efforts, peace efforts. "In an effort to" is a useful formal alternative to "in order to try to".

expressions.usage: Without thinking, because you always do it

expressions.az: bir şeyi etməyə vərdiş etmək, adətkar olmaq

expressions.usage: sleep = rest with your eyes closed, as at night
regular = happening often or at the same time each day

sentences.en: I only smoke out of habit.
sentences.az: Mən yalnız vərdiş üzrə siqaret çəkirəm.

sentences.en: He has an annoying habit of interrupting people.
sentences.az: Onun insanların sözünü kəsmək kimi əsəbiləşdirən vərdişi var.

sentences.en: She is in the habit of getting up early.
sentences.az: O, tez durmağa vərdiş edib.

sentences.en: My grandfather is a creature of habit: he has lunch at one o'clock every day.
sentences.az: Babam vərdişlərindən əl çəkməyən adamdır: hər gün saat birdə nahar edir.

usage: A HABIT is something one person does regularly, often without thinking (a bad habit, eating habits). A CUSTOM is a traditional practice of a society (a local custom). Both can be "adət" in Azerbaijani, so choose carefully. Verbs: have a habit, get into / develop a habit, break / kick a habit. The pattern is "a habit OF doing something", not "a habit to do".

expressions.usage: unique = being the only one of its kind

expressions.az: fürsətdən istifadə etmək, fürsəti əldən verməmək

expressions.usage: Fixed phrase = as soon as possible

sentences.en: The course gives students an opportunity to practise their English.
sentences.az: Kurs tələbələrə ingilis dilini məşq etmək imkanı verir.

sentences.en: Don't miss this golden opportunity.
sentences.az: Bu qızıl fürsəti əldən vermə.

sentences.en: She seized the opportunity to study abroad.
sentences.az: O, xaricdə təhsil almaq fürsətindən istifadə etdi.

sentences.en: I will call you at the first opportunity.
sentences.az: İlk fürsətdə sənə zəng edəcəyəm.

usage: OPPORTUNITY and CHANCE are close, but OPPORTUNITY is more formal and always positive: a situation in which it is possible to do something you want. CHANCE also means possibility or luck ("There is a chance of rain", "by chance"); OPPORTUNITY cannot be used that way. Do not say "a possibility to do": say "an opportunity to do" or "a chance to do". Verbs: have, get, take, seize, miss, give, offer.

expressions.az: sınaqdan üzüağ çıxmaq, çətinliyin öhdəsindən gəlmək

expressions.usage: pose = create (a problem that must be dealt with); formal
exciting = causing great interest and enthusiasm
belief = something you think is true

sentences.en: Finding a job was a real challenge.
sentences.az: İş tapmaq əsl sınaq idi.

sentences.en: Climate change poses a major challenge to all countries.
sentences.az: İqlim dəyişikliyi bütün ölkələr üçün ciddi çağırışdır.

sentences.en: I am sure she will rise to the challenge.
sentences.az: Əminəm ki, o, bu sınaqdan üzüağ çıxacaq.

sentences.en: The new job is difficult, but I find it challenging.
sentences.az: Yeni iş çətindir, amma mənə maraqlıdır.

usage: A CHALLENGE is something difficult that tests your ability, and the word is positive compared with PROBLEM or DIFFICULTY: people "enjoy a challenge". The usual verb is FACE a challenge; also meet, accept, rise to, overcome. As a verb, CHALLENGE means to question whether something is right (challenge a decision) or to invite somebody to compete (challenge him to a game). CHALLENGING is a polite, positive way to say "difficult".

expressions.usage: work under pressure; be under pressure TO do something
peer = a person of the same age or status
blood = the red liquid in your body
air = the mixture of gases around the Earth
resist = refuse to accept or be changed by

sentences.en: I work well under pressure.
sentences.az: Mən gərgin şəraitdə yaxşı işləyirəm.

sentences.en: Teenagers often start smoking because of peer pressure.
sentences.az: Yeniyetmələr çox vaxt yaşıdlarının təsiri ilə siqaret çəkməyə başlayırlar.

sentences.en: He has high blood pressure.
sentences.az: Onun qan təzyiqi yüksəkdir.

sentences.en: How do you cope with the pressure of exams?
sentences.az: İmtahan gərginliyinin öhdəsindən necə gəlirsən?

usage: PRESSURE is uncountable in most uses ("a lot of pressure"), though the plural appears in "the pressures of modern life". Key verbs: PUT pressure ON somebody (to do something), be / come UNDER pressure, cope with / handle pressure, relieve / take the pressure off. PRESSURE comes from outside (a boss, exams, deadlines); STRESS is the feeling inside you that results from it.

expressions.usage: behaviour = the way a person acts
deny = say that something is not true

sentences.en: Who is responsible for this department?
sentences.az: Bu şöbəyə kim cavabdehdir?

sentences.en: Parents are responsible for their children's safety.
sentences.az: Valideynlər övladlarının təhlükəsizliyinə cavabdehdirlər.

sentences.en: The company denied responsibility for the accident.
sentences.az: Şirkət qəzaya görə məsuliyyəti boynuna almadı.

sentences.en: She has a strong sense of responsibility.
sentences.az: Onda güclü məsuliyyət hissi var.

usage: RESPONSIBLE has two uses. Before a noun it means sensible and reliable: "a responsible person". After a verb with FOR it means in charge of, or to blame for: "responsible for sales", "responsible for the damage". The spelling ends in -IBLE, not -able. Noun patterns: TAKE responsibility FOR something; have a responsibility TO somebody. Azerbaijani "cavabdeh" and "məsuliyyətli" are both RESPONSIBLE.

expressions.az: nəyəsə əmin, bir şey barədə inamlı
expressions.usage: confident ABOUT the future / the exam

expressions.usage: reasonably = to a fairly high degree
tell somebody something in confidence = as a secret

sentences.en: I feel confident about the exam.
sentences.az: Mən imtahana görə özümə əminəm.

sentences.en: Passing the test really boosted my confidence.
sentences.az: Testdən keçmək özünəinamımı həqiqətən artırdı.

sentences.en: She is not confident enough to speak in public.
sentences.az: O, camaat qarşısında danışacaq qədər özünə inamlı deyil.

sentences.en: I am telling you this in confidence.
sentences.az: Bunu sənə sirr olaraq deyirəm.

usage: CONFIDENT describes a feeling of being sure, either of yourself ("a confident speaker") or of a fact ("I'm confident that we will win"). Prepositions: confident ABOUT / OF something, confidence IN somebody. Do not confuse CONFIDENT with CONFIDENTIAL (secret): "in confidence" belongs to that second meaning. Verbs with CONFIDENCE: gain, build, boost, lose, lack, restore.

expressions.usage: illness = the state of being ill

expressions.az: bir şeyə ciddi yanaşmaq, ciddi fikirli olmaq

expressions.usage: attempt = an act of trying to do something

sentences.en: Is he serious about leaving his job?
sentences.az: O, işdən çıxmaq barədə ciddidir?

sentences.en: Pollution is a serious threat to our health.
sentences.az: Çirklənmə sağlamlığımız üçün ciddi təhlükədir.

sentences.en: I have serious doubts about this plan.
sentences.az: Bu planla bağlı ciddi şübhələrim var.

usage: SERIOUS means bad or dangerous with problems (a serious illness, a serious mistake), and sincere, not joking, with people ("Are you serious?"). SERIOUSLY is common in three ways: with adjectives for bad states (seriously ill), in "take something seriously" (bir şeyə ciddi yanaşmaq), and at the start of a spoken sentence to show you are not joking. For large amounts, use "considerable" or "significant", not "serious".

sentences.az: O, iyirmi beş yaşında öz şirkətini qurdu.

sentences.en: Try to set aside some time for reading every day.
sentences.az: Hər gün mütaliə üçün bir az vaxt ayırmağa çalış.

usage: SET is irregular and never changes: set – set – set. Its core idea is "put something in a fixed position or state": set a date, set a limit, set a record, set an example. With particles it forms very common phrasal verbs: set off (leave), set up (establish), set out (begin with a purpose), set aside (save). As a noun, a SET is a group of things that belong together: a set of keys, a chess set.

Phrasal verb: run away from home
Phrasal verb: We have run out of milk
Idiom; long = lasting a great amount of time
errand = a short trip to buy or deliver something
run FOR + position = try to be elected

sentences.az: O, öz biznesini idarə edir.

sentences.az: Benzinimiz qurtarıb.

sentences.en: I ran into an old friend at the airport.
sentences.az: Hava limanında köhnə bir dostuma rast gəldim.

sentences.en: It will save you money in the long run.
sentences.az: Bu, uzun müddətdə sənə pul qənaət etdirəcək.

usage: RUN is irregular: run – ran – run. Beyond the physical meaning, three uses are essential: 1) manage or organise – run a business, run a course; 2) operate – "The engine is running", "run a program"; 3) of transport – "The buses run every ten minutes". Phrasal verbs: run out of (have none left), run into (meet by chance), run away (escape). "In the long run" contrasts with "in the short run".

expressions.usage: Do you have anything in mind?
never = not at any time; fixed spoken phrase
Do you mind if I ...? / Do you mind + -ing?
state = the condition somebody is in
British idiom: be in two minds about something
slip = slide; "It slipped my mind" = I forgot

sentences.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
sentences.az: Pəncərəni açsam, etiraz etməzsiniz?

sentences.en: I'm sorry I'm late. – Never mind.
sentences.az: Bağışlayın, gecikdim. – Eybi yoxdur.

sentences.en: Tea or coffee? – I don't mind.
sentences.az: Çay, yoxsa qəhvə? – Mənə fərqi yoxdur.

sentences.en: I'm in two minds about accepting the job.
sentences.az: İşi qəbul edib-etməmək barədə tərəddüd edirəm.

usage: As a noun, MIND is the part of you that thinks and remembers; it is close to "ağıl" and "fikir", not to BRAIN (the physical organ). Key idioms: change your mind (fikrini dəyişmək), make up your mind (qərara gəlmək), keep / bear in mind (yadda saxlamaq). As a verb it means to object: "Do you mind + -ing?" is a polite request, and the polite positive answer is "No, not at all". "Mind the gap!" is a warning.

Spoken; said when you accept an offer

sentences.az: Çətin müştərilərlə necə davranırsan?

sentences.en: The two companies have struck a deal.
sentences.az: İki şirkət razılıq əldə edib.

sentences.en: I'll cook if you wash the dishes. – It's a deal!
sentences.az: Sən qabları yusan, mən yemək bişirərəm. – Razılaşdıq!

sentences.en: The staff are trained to deal with emergencies.
sentences.az: Heyət fövqəladə vəziyyətlərin öhdəsindən gəlmək üçün təlim keçib.

usage: DEAL is irregular: deal – dealt – dealt, pronounced /delt/. DEAL WITH has three meanings: take action to solve (deal with a problem), do business with (deal with a supplier) and be about (The book deals with war). The noun DEAL is a business agreement; "a great deal of" means "a lot of" and is used with uncountable nouns in formal English: a great deal of money. "It's no big deal" means it is not important.

expressions.usage: statistical = based on numbers that show facts
sample = a small amount tested to learn about the whole
critical = judging the good and bad points carefully
political = connected with government and public affairs
ability = the skill or power to do something
pattern = the regular way in which something happens

sentences.en: Researchers analysed data from more than fifty countries.
sentences.az: Tədqiqatçılar əllidən çox ölkənin məlumatlarını təhlil ediblər.

sentences.en: The report provides a thorough analysis of the housing market.
sentences.az: Hesabatda mənzil bazarının hərtərəfli təhlili verilir.

sentences.en: Blood samples were sent to the laboratory to be analysed.
sentences.az: Qan nümunələri təhlil olunmaq üçün laboratoriyaya göndərildi.

sentences.en: The job requires strong analytical ability.
sentences.az: Bu iş güclü analitik qabiliyyət tələb edir.

usage: ANALYSE is the British spelling; American English writes "analyze". The noun ANALYSIS has the irregular plural ANALYSES /əˈnæləsiːz/. Notice how the stress moves through the family: ANalyse, aNALysis, ANalyst, anaLYTical. In academic writing you "carry out" or "conduct" an analysis OF something; "in the final analysis" means "when everything has been considered".

expressions.usage: value = how much something is worth
continuous = without stopping; marks given for work during the course
candidate = a person applying for a job or taking an exam
progress = movement towards a better state; uncountable
objectively = without being influenced by personal feelings
patient = a person receiving medical treatment

sentences.en: It is too early to assess the effects of the new law.
sentences.az: Yeni qanunun təsirlərini qiymətləndirmək hələ tezdir.

sentences.en: Students are judged by continuous assessment rather than by a final exam.
sentences.az: Tələbələr yekun imtahanla deyil, cari qiymətləndirmə ilə dəyərləndirilirlər.

sentences.en: The nurse assessed the patient before the doctor arrived.
sentences.az: Tibb bacısı həkim gələnə qədər xəstənin vəziyyətini qiymətləndirdi.

sentences.en: Teachers meet every month to assess the progress of each pupil.
sentences.az: Müəllimlər hər bir şagirdin irəliləyişini qiymətləndirmək üçün hər ay görüşürlər.

usage: ASSESS means to form a careful judgement about the quality, size or importance of something. It is more formal than "judge" and more general than "evaluate", which suggests a systematic study. Patterns: assess something; assess whether / how / what + clause; be assessed AT + amount ("The damage was assessed at two million pounds"). In education, ASSESSMENT covers tests, coursework and exams.

expressions.usage: underlying = existing under the surface; basic but not stated
command = control over a group, especially soldiers; here "assume" = take
