expressions.usage: widely = by many people; impersonal academic pattern

sentences.en: I assumed that you knew each other.
sentences.az: Mən güman edirdim ki, siz bir-birinizi tanıyırsınız.

sentences.en: Don't automatically assume that expensive products are better.
sentences.az: Avtomatik olaraq güman etməyin ki, bahalı məhsullar daha yaxşıdır.

sentences.en: The plan was based on the assumption that prices would continue to rise.
sentences.az: Plan qiymətlərin artmaqda davam edəcəyi fərziyyəsinə əsaslanırdı.

sentences.en: It is widely assumed that the minister will resign.
sentences.az: Çoxları nazirin istefa verəcəyini güman edir.

usage: ASSUME means to accept that something is true without proof. PRESUME is close, but suggests you have some reason; SUPPOSE is more informal. "Assuming (that) ..." works like "if": "Assuming the weather is good, we'll leave at six." In formal English ASSUME also means to take a position or duty: assume responsibility, assume office, assume control.

sentences.en: There is no scientific evidence that the diet works.
sentences.az: Bu pəhrizin təsirli olduğuna dair heç bir elmi sübut yoxdur.

sentences.en: The police did not have sufficient evidence to arrest him.
sentences.az: Polisin onu həbs etmək üçün kifayət qədər sübutu yox idi.

sentences.en: It is evident that the system needs to be changed.
sentences.az: Aydındır ki, sistem dəyişdirilməlidir.

sentences.en: The jury must weigh the evidence before reaching a decision.
sentences.az: Andlılar qərar verməzdən əvvəl sübutları ölçüb-biçməlidirlər.

usage: EVIDENCE is uncountable: "a lot of evidence", "a piece of evidence" – never "an evidence" or "evidences". Prepositions: evidence OF / FOR something, evidence THAT + clause, evidence AGAINST somebody. PROOF is stronger: evidence makes you believe something, proof shows it is definitely true. In essays, "There is growing evidence that ..." and "The evidence suggests that ..." are safe, cautious ways to introduce a claim.

expressions.usage: Linker; as a consequence OF + noun
regardless of = paying no attention to

sentences.en: Many people lost their jobs as a consequence of the crisis.
sentences.az: Böhran nəticəsində bir çox insan işini itirdi.

sentences.en: If you break the rules, you will have to suffer the consequences.
sentences.az: Qaydaları pozsan, nəticələrinə qatlaşmalı olacaqsan.

sentences.en: The decision could have far-reaching consequences for the whole region.
sentences.az: Bu qərarın bütün region üçün genişmiqyaslı nəticələri ola bilər.

sentences.en: Demand fell and, consequently, prices dropped.
sentences.az: Tələbat azaldı və nəticədə qiymətlər düşdü.

usage: CONSEQUENCE is usually plural and usually negative; a neutral word is RESULT and a positive one is BENEFIT. Prepositions: the consequences OF an action FOR a person or thing. CONSEQUENTLY is a formal linker meaning "as a result" and is followed by a comma at the start of a sentence. "Of little consequence" (formal) means "not important". Typical verbs: have, face, suffer, accept, consider the consequences.

expressions.usage: The basic pattern: have an impact ON something
considerable = large enough to be important
negative = bad or harmful; opposite: positive
minimise = reduce to the lowest possible level
tourism = the business of providing services for visitors

sentences.en: Social media has had an enormous impact on the way we communicate.
sentences.az: Sosial media ünsiyyət tərzimizə çox böyük təsir göstərib.

sentences.en: The new tax will have a negative impact on small businesses.
sentences.az: Yeni vergi kiçik müəssisələrə mənfi təsir göstərəcək.

sentences.en: The government is trying to minimise the impact of rising prices.
sentences.az: Hökumət artan qiymətlərin təsirini minimuma endirməyə çalışır.

sentences.en: The essay examines the impact of tourism on the local environment.
sentences.az: Essedə turizmin yerli ətraf mühitə təsiri araşdırılır.

usage: The noun is stressed on the first syllable (IMpact), the verb on the second (imPACT). The noun pattern is "have / make an impact ON something" – not "to" or "in". IMPACT is stronger than EFFECT or INFLUENCE and suggests a powerful, noticeable result. As a verb ("impact on prices") it is common in business and journalism, but many writers prefer "affect" in formal essays. "On impact" means at the moment when one object hits another.

lessons.azerbaijani: məsələ, problem; (jurnal) buraxılış, nömrə; rəsmən vermək, dərc etmək

expressions.usage: raise = mention a subject for discussion
sensitive = needing careful treatment because it may upset people
complex = having many parts and difficult to understand
ethical = connected with principles of right and wrong
statement = a formal announcement; here "issue" is a verb
warning = a statement that something bad may happen

sentences.en: Several parents raised the issue of safety at the meeting.
sentences.az: İclasda bir neçə valideyn təhlükəsizlik məsələsini qaldırdı.

sentences.en: Unemployment is the most pressing issue facing the country.
sentences.az: İşsizlik ölkənin üzləşdiyi ən təxirəsalınmaz məsələdir.

sentences.en: The company issued a statement denying the report.
sentences.az: Şirkət bu xəbəri təkzib edən bəyanat yaydı.

sentences.en: Immigration is a complex and sensitive issue.
sentences.az: İmmiqrasiya mürəkkəb və həssas məsələdir.

usage: An ISSUE is an important subject that people discuss or argue about; it is more neutral than PROBLEM, which is why it is the preferred word in essays ("environmental issues"). The verb means to give out officially: issue a passport, a statement, a warning. Another meaning is one number of a magazine ("the March issue"). "Take issue with somebody" (formal) means to disagree; "the point at issue" is the subject being discussed.

expressions.usage: upward = moving towards a higher level
downward = moving towards a lower level
recent = that happened a short time ago
reverse = change something to its opposite
general = affecting most people or things
population = all the people living in a country or area

sentences.en: The graph shows an upward trend in the number of students studying abroad.
sentences.az: Qrafik xaricdə təhsil alan tələbələrin sayında artım meylini göstərir.

sentences.en: If current trends continue, the city will need thousands of new homes.
sentences.az: Hazırkı meyllər davam edərsə, şəhərə minlərlə yeni ev lazım olacaq.

sentences.en: The government hopes to reverse the downward trend in birth rates.
sentences.az: Hökumət doğum səviyyəsindəki azalma meylini dəyişməyə ümid edir.

sentences.en: There is a general trend towards working from home.
sentences.az: Evdən işləməyə doğru ümumi bir meyil var.

usage: A TREND is a general direction in which a situation is changing. It is essential vocabulary for describing graphs in IELTS Writing Task 1: an upward / downward trend IN something; a trend TOWARDS something. In everyday English a trend is also a fashion ("the latest trends"), and TRENDY is an informal adjective for fashionable places and people. "Set a trend" means to start something that others copy.

expressions.usage: adopt = start to use a method
flexible = able to change to suit new conditions
systematic = done according to a careful plan
step-by-step = dealing with one thing at a time
radical = new and very different from what is usual
rapidly = very quickly; here "approach" is a verb

sentences.en: The school has adopted a new approach to teaching languages.
sentences.az: Məktəb dillərin tədrisinə yeni yanaşma tətbiq edib.

sentences.en: We need a more flexible approach to working hours.
sentences.az: İş saatlarına daha çevik yanaşmaya ehtiyacımız var.

sentences.en: The deadline is rapidly approaching.
sentences.az: Son müddət sürətlə yaxınlaşır.

sentences.en: As we approached the village, it started to rain.
sentences.az: Biz kəndə yaxınlaşanda yağış yağmağa başladı.

usage: As a noun, APPROACH means a way of dealing with something and takes TO: "an approach TO the problem" (not "of" or "for"). As a verb it takes a direct object with no preposition: "We approached the town" – never "approached to the town". You can also approach a person (speak to them about a request) or approach a task (begin to deal with it). Typical verbs: adopt, take, try, develop an approach.

expressions.usage: indicate = show that something is true
market = the people who might buy a product
grant = money given by an organisation for a purpose
publish = print and make available to the public
field = an area of study or activity
leading = most important or most successful

sentences.en: She is conducting research into the causes of the disease.
sentences.az: O, xəstəliyin səbəblərini tədqiq edir.

sentences.en: Recent research indicates that sleep improves memory.
sentences.az: Son tədqiqatlar yuxunun yaddaşı yaxşılaşdırdığını göstərir.

sentences.en: The university received a research grant of two million pounds.
sentences.az: Universitet iki milyon funt məbləğində tədqiqat qrantı aldı.

sentences.en: He is one of the leading researchers in his field.
sentences.az: O, öz sahəsinin aparıcı tədqiqatçılarından biridir.

usage: RESEARCH is uncountable: "some research", "a piece of research" – not "a research" or "many researches". The usual verbs are DO, CARRY OUT and CONDUCT (never "make research"). Prepositions: research INTO / ON a subject. Both stress patterns are heard in British English: reSEARCH and REsearch. In essays, "Research shows / indicates / suggests that ..." is a standard way to support a claim.

expressions.usage: proportion = a part of a whole
shift = a change in position or direction
minority = the smaller part of a group
factor = one of the things that cause a result

sentences.en: A significant proportion of the population lives in cities.
sentences.az: Əhalinin əhəmiyyətli hissəsi şəhərlərdə yaşayır.

sentences.en: There was a significant decline in sales last year.
sentences.az: Keçən il satışlarda nəzərəçarpan azalma oldu.

sentences.en: The weather can significantly affect our mood.
sentences.az: Hava əhval-ruhiyyəmizə xeyli dərəcədə təsir edə bilər.

sentences.en: Cost was a significant factor in our decision.
sentences.az: Qiymət qərarımızda mühüm amil idi.

usage: SIGNIFICANT means large or important enough to be noticed, and it is the standard academic alternative to "big" or "important": a significant increase, a significant difference. SIGNIFICANTLY is frequent in descriptions of data: "significantly higher", "rose significantly". In statistics, "statistically significant" means unlikely to be the result of chance. Remember that AFFECT is the verb and EFFECT is the noun.

expressions.usage: stage = a period in a process
element = a necessary part of something
distinction = a clear difference between similar things
aspect = one part or side of a situation
component = one of the parts of a system

sentences.en: The talks have reached a crucial stage.
sentences.az: Danışıqlar həlledici mərhələyə çatıb.

sentences.en: Trust is a crucial element of any relationship.
sentences.az: Etimad istənilən münasibətin ən vacib ünsürüdür.

sentences.en: It is crucial that we act now.
sentences.az: İndi hərəkətə keçməyimiz son dərəcə vacibdir.

sentences.en: Her experience proved crucial to the success of the project.
sentences.az: Onun təcrübəsi layihənin uğuru üçün həlledici oldu.

usage: CRUCIAL is an "extreme" adjective meaning extremely important because other things depend on it. Because it is already strong, do not say "very crucial"; use "absolutely crucial". Patterns: crucial TO / FOR something; it is crucial THAT ...; play a crucial role IN. Near synonyms: VITAL, ESSENTIAL, CRITICAL. In IELTS essays it is a good replacement for "very important".

lessons.azerbaijani: sərmayə qoymaq, investisiya yatırmaq; (vaxt, güc) sərf etmək

expressions.az: xarici sərmayə (xaricdən gələn və ya xaricə yönələn)
expressions.usage: overseas = in or from foreign countries
stock = a share in the ownership of a company
return = the profit you get; often shortened to ROI
infrastructure = roads, bridges, power supplies and other basic systems

sentences.en: The government has invested heavily in public transport.
sentences.az: Hökumət ictimai nəqliyyata böyük sərmayə qoyub.

sentences.en: The region needs to attract more overseas investment.
sentences.az: Region daha çox xarici sərmayə cəlb etməlidir.

sentences.en: Buying a flat in the city centre was a good investment.
sentences.az: Şəhərin mərkəzində mənzil almaq yaxşı sərmayə idi.

sentences.en: You have to invest a lot of time in learning a language.
sentences.az: Dil öyrənməyə çoxlu vaxt sərf etməlisən.

usage: INVEST always takes IN: "invest IN shares", "invest money IN a business" – not "invest to". It is also used for time, energy and effort. INVESTMENT is uncountable for the activity ("foreign investment") and countable for a particular sum or thing ("a good investment"). An INVESTOR is a person or organisation that invests.

expressions.usage: enter = put your name down for
rival = a person or company competing with another
salary = money paid every month for a job

sentences.en: Small shops cannot compete with the big supermarkets.
sentences.az: Kiçik mağazalar iri supermarketlərlə rəqabət apara bilmir.

sentences.en: Ten companies are competing for the contract.
sentences.az: On şirkət müqavilə uğrunda rəqabət aparır.

sentences.en: There is fierce competition for places at the best universities.
sentences.az: Ən yaxşı universitetlərdə yer uğrunda kəskin rəqabət var.

sentences.en: She will compete in the Olympics next year.
sentences.az: O, gələn il Olimpiya oyunlarında yarışacaq.

usage: Prepositions decide the meaning: compete WITH / AGAINST a rival, compete FOR a prize, compete IN a race or market. COMPETITION is uncountable for the situation of rivalry ("fierce competition") and countable for an organised event ("enter a competition"). "The competition" can also mean your rivals as a group. COMPETITIVE describes prices and salaries that are as good as others, and people who want to win.

lessons.azerbaijani: istehlak etmək, sərf etmək; yemək, içmək

expressions.usage: energy = power from electricity, fuel, etc.
goods = things produced to be sold; plural noun
fuel = material burned to produce heat or power
society = people living together in an organised community
calorie = a unit for measuring the energy in food
preference = a greater liking for one thing
excessive = more than is necessary or reasonable

sentences.en: Old fridges consume a lot of energy.
sentences.az: Köhnə soyuducular çoxlu enerji sərf edir.

sentences.en: The new engine has much lower fuel consumption.
sentences.az: Yeni mühərrikin yanacaq sərfiyyatı xeyli azdır.

sentences.en: We live in a consumer society where people buy more than they need.
sentences.az: Biz insanların ehtiyacından artıq aldığı istehlak cəmiyyətində yaşayırıq.

sentences.en: Excessive consumption of sugar is bad for your health.
sentences.az: Həddindən artıq şəkər istehlakı sağlamlığa zərərlidir.

usage: CONSUME is the formal word for "use" (energy, fuel, time, resources) and for "eat or drink" (consume alcohol, consume calories). The noun CONSUMPTION drops the "e" and adds "p": consume – consumption. CONSUMER appears before many nouns: consumer goods, consumer rights, consumer demand. "Be consumed by / with" a feeling (guilt, anger) means to be filled with it. TIME-CONSUMING describes tasks that take a long time.

adj.az: çox zəhmət tələb edən, həmçinin tələbkar

expressions.usage: high = great in amount or level
supply = the amount of something that is available
apology = saying that you are sorry
boss = the person in charge of you at work
refund = money paid back to a customer
drop = a fall to a lower level

sentences.en: The factory cannot satisfy the demand for its products.
sentences.az: Zavod məhsullarına olan tələbatı ödəyə bilmir.

sentences.en: Good teachers are always in high demand.
sentences.az: Yaxşı müəllimlərə həmişə böyük tələbat var.

sentences.en: Prices are decided by supply and demand.
sentences.az: Qiymətləri tələb və təklif müəyyən edir.

sentences.en: The customer demanded a refund.
sentences.az: Müştəri pulun geri qaytarılmasını tələb etdi.

usage: As a noun, DEMAND takes FOR: "the demand FOR oil". As a verb it takes a direct object with no preposition: "They demanded an explanation" – not "demanded for". The verb is strong, almost aggressive; for polite situations use "ask for" or "request". Patterns: demand THAT somebody (should) do something; demand TO know. DEMANDING describes work that needs a lot of effort and people who expect a lot.

lessons.azerbaijani: mənfəət, qazanc, gəlir; qazanc əldə etmək, faydalanmaq

expressions.usage: sell something at a profit; opposite: at a loss
margin = the difference between cost and selling price
net = remaining after tax and costs are taken away
gross = total, before anything is taken away
annual = for a period of one year
venture = a new business activity involving risk
organisation = a group with a particular purpose
maximise = increase as much as possible

sentences.en: We sold the house at a profit.
sentences.az: Biz evi qazancla satdıq.

sentences.en: The company's net profit rose by eight per cent.
sentences.az: Şirkətin xalis mənfəəti səkkiz faiz artdı.

sentences.en: Supermarkets work with very small profit margins.
sentences.az: Supermarketlər çox kiçik mənfəət marjası ilə işləyir.

sentences.en: She works for a non-profit organisation that helps refugees.
sentences.az: O, qaçqınlara kömək edən qeyri-kommersiya təşkilatında işləyir.

usage: PROFIT is the money left after costs have been paid; the opposite is LOSS. The usual verbs are MAKE a profit and, more formally, EARN, GENERATE or REPORT a profit. It can be countable or uncountable ("a profit of one million pounds", "sell at a profit"). GROSS profit is before tax and costs, NET profit after them. As a verb: profit FROM something. Do not confuse PROFIT with BENEFIT (an advantage, not necessarily money).

expressions.usage: recovery = the process of returning to a normal state
downturn = a fall in business activity
reform = a change made to improve a system

sentences.en: Tourism plays an important role in the national economy.
sentences.az: Turizm milli iqtisadiyyatda mühüm rol oynayır.

sentences.en: There are signs of economic recovery.
sentences.az: İqtisadi dirçəliş əlamətləri var.

sentences.en: The government cut taxes to stimulate the economy.
sentences.az: Hökumət iqtisadiyyatı canlandırmaq üçün vergiləri azaltdı.

sentences.en: She has a degree in economics from Baku State University.
sentences.az: Onun Bakı Dövlət Universitetindən iqtisadiyyat üzrə diplomu var.

usage: Do not confuse ECONOMIC (connected with the economy: economic growth, economic policy) with ECONOMICAL (not wasting money or fuel: an economical car). ECONOMICS, the subject, looks plural but takes a singular verb: "Economics is my favourite subject." Stress shifts through the family: eCONomy, ecoNOMic, eCONomist. "Economy class" is the cheapest type of air ticket.

expressions.usage: natural = existing in nature, not made by people
scarce = not enough for everyone who needs it
finite = having a limit or end
renewable = that can be replaced naturally
precious = rare and worth a lot
mineral = a substance found naturally in the earth

expressions.az: ehtiyatlardan istifadə etmək, onları istismar etmək

expressions.usage: conserve = use as little as possible

sentences.en: Azerbaijan is rich in natural resources such as oil and gas.
sentences.az: Azərbaycan neft və qaz kimi təbii sərvətlərlə zəngindir.

sentences.en: Water is a precious resource in dry countries.
sentences.az: Quraq ölkələrdə su qiymətli sərvətdir.

sentences.en: We must conserve the planet's finite resources.
sentences.az: Planetin tükənən ehtiyatlarına qənaət etməliyik.

sentences.en: The school does not have the resources to buy new computers.
sentences.az: Məktəbin yeni kompüterlər almaq üçün vəsaiti yoxdur.

usage: RESOURCE is usually plural. It covers natural wealth (oil, water, forests), money and materials available to an organisation ("limited resources"), and useful materials for study ("teaching resources"). HUMAN RESOURCES (HR) is the department that deals with employees. RESOURCEFUL describes a person who is good at finding ways of solving problems. Do not confuse RESOURCE with SOURCE (the place something comes from).

expressions.usage: pursue = continue to follow a plan over time
strict = that must be obeyed exactly
immigration = coming to live permanently in another country
zero-tolerance = punishing even the smallest offence
monetary = connected with money, especially a country's money supply

sentences.en: The president made a speech on foreign policy.
sentences.az: Prezident xarici siyasətlə bağlı çıxış etdi.

sentences.en: The school has a strict policy on mobile phones.
sentences.az: Məktəbin mobil telefonlarla bağlı sərt qaydası var.

sentences.en: The government was forced to abandon the policy.
sentences.az: Hökumət bu siyasətdən imtina etməyə məcbur oldu.

sentences.en: The central bank is responsible for monetary policy.
sentences.az: Mərkəzi bank pul-kredit siyasətinə cavabdehdir.

usage: Azerbaijani "siyasət" covers two English words. POLITICS is the activity of government and the struggle for power ("She went into politics"); a POLICY is a plan or set of rules chosen by a government, company or school ("the company's policy on holidays"). The preposition is ON: a policy ON education. A policy is also an insurance contract: "an insurance policy". "Honesty is the best policy" is a proverb.

expressions.usage: proposal = a formal plan or suggestion
remark = something that you say; a comment
spark = cause something to start suddenly
scheme = an official plan; British English

sentences.en: The minister's controversial remarks angered many teachers.
sentences.az: Nazirin mübahisə doğuran sözləri bir çox müəllimi qəzəbləndirdi.

sentences.en: The new law has sparked controversy across the country.
sentences.az: Yeni qanun bütün ölkədə mübahisə doğurub.

sentences.en: He remains a controversial figure in British politics.
sentences.az: O, Britaniya siyasətində birmənalı qarşılanmayan şəxsiyyət olaraq qalır.

sentences.en: The controversy surrounding the film helped to sell tickets.
sentences.az: Filmin ətrafında yaranan mübahisə biletlərin satılmasına kömək etdi.

usage: CONTROVERSIAL describes something that causes strong public disagreement; it does not mean "wrong". British speakers stress the noun in two ways: CONtroversy and conTROVersy. Verbs with the noun: cause, spark, stir up, arouse controversy; a controversy arises. In IELTS essays, "a controversial issue" and "this remains controversial" are useful for introducing a debate.

expressions.usage: launch = start an activity, especially an organised one
election = choosing a person for a position by voting
advertising = telling the public about products
racism = unfair treatment of people of other races
fundraising = collecting money for a charity or cause
slogan = a short phrase that is easy to remember
nationwide = happening in all parts of a country
tireless = working very hard without stopping

sentences.en: The government has launched a campaign to reduce smoking.
sentences.az: Hökumət siqaretçəkmənin azaldılması üçün kampaniyaya başlayıb.

sentences.en: The party spent millions on its election campaign.
sentences.az: Partiya seçki kampaniyasına milyonlar xərclədi.

sentences.en: She has campaigned against racism all her life.
sentences.az: O, bütün ömrü boyu irqçiliyə qarşı mübarizə aparıb.

sentences.en: He was a tireless campaigner for children's rights.
sentences.az: O, uşaq hüquqları uğrunda yorulmaz mübariz idi.

usage: The "g" in CAMPAIGN is silent: /kæmˈpeɪn/. A campaign is a planned series of activities with a particular aim: political, commercial or social. As a verb it takes FOR or AGAINST: campaign FOR equal pay, campaign AGAINST a new road. Typical verbs with the noun: launch, run, lead, mount, support a campaign.

lessons.azerbaijani: davam etdirmək, qoruyub saxlamaq; (zərər, xəsarət) almaq

adj.az: davamlı olmayan, belə davam edə bilməyən

expressions.usage: source = a place or thing that you get something from
material = a substance that things are made from
momentum = the force that keeps a process developing
pace = the speed at which something happens
attack = an act of violence or strong criticism

expressions.az: son nəticədə davam etdirilməsi mümkün olmayan

expressions.usage: commitment = a promise to support something

sentences.en: We need to get more of our energy from sustainable sources.
sentences.az: Enerjimizin daha çox hissəsini davamlı mənbələrdən əldə etməliyik.

sentences.en: The team could not sustain the pace in the second half.
sentences.az: Komanda ikinci hissədə tempi saxlaya bilmədi.

sentences.en: Such high levels of debt are ultimately unsustainable.
sentences.az: Borcun belə yüksək səviyyəsi son nəticədə davam edə bilməz.

sentences.en: Two passengers sustained serious injuries in the crash.
sentences.az: Qəzada iki sərnişin ağır xəsarət aldı.

usage: SUSTAIN has three uses: 1) make something continue (sustain growth, sustain interest); 2) formally, suffer something bad (sustain an injury, sustain damage); 3) keep alive (enough food to sustain life). SUSTAINABLE is a key word for environmental topics: sustainable development means economic growth that does not destroy natural resources. SUSTAINED is the adjective for something that continues for a long time: a sustained effort.

expressions.usage: technique = a particular way of doing something that needs skill
feature = an important part or quality of something
strategy = a plan intended to achieve a purpose
encourage = give support and hope to
hub = the central point of an activity
embrace = accept an idea with enthusiasm

sentences.en: Companies must constantly innovate to stay ahead of their rivals.
sentences.az: Şirkətlər rəqiblərini qabaqlamaq üçün daim yenilik etməlidirlər.

sentences.en: The phone has several innovative features.
sentences.az: Telefonun bir neçə yenilikçi funksiyası var.

sentences.en: The city has become a hub of innovation.
sentences.az: Şəhər innovasiya mərkəzinə çevrilib.

sentences.en: Lower taxes are intended to encourage innovation.
sentences.az: Aşağı vergilər yenilikləri təşviq etmək məqsədi daşıyır.

usage: INNOVATE means to introduce new ideas, methods or products; it is usually intransitive. An INVENTION is a completely new thing; an INNOVATION may be a new way of using existing things. The adjective INNOVATIVE is pronounced /ˈɪnəvətɪv/ or /ˈɪnəveɪtɪv/. INNOVATION is uncountable for the process ("encourage innovation") and countable for a single new idea ("the latest innovations").

expressions.usage: mild = not very cold or very hot
tropical = of the hottest parts of the world
fear = the feeling of being afraid; figurative use of "climate"
summit = an official meeting between leaders
greenhouse = a glass building for plants; gas = a substance like air
carbon = the element in coal and CO2; footprint = the mark left by a foot

sentences.en: Lankaran has a mild, humid climate.
sentences.az: Lənkəranın mülayim, rütubətli iqlimi var.

sentences.en: Climate change is the greatest threat facing our planet.
sentences.az: İqlim dəyişikliyi planetimizin üzləşdiyi ən böyük təhlükədir.

sentences.en: World leaders will meet at the climate summit in November.
sentences.az: Dünya liderləri noyabrda iqlim sammitində görüşəcəklər.

sentences.en: You can reduce your carbon footprint by flying less.
sentences.az: Daha az uçmaqla karbon izinizi azalda bilərsiniz.

usage: WEATHER is what happens today (rain, sun); CLIMATE is the typical weather of a place over many years. "Climate change" is the fixed term for long-term changes in the Earth's temperature; "global warming" is one part of it. CLIMATE is also used figuratively for the general mood or situation: the political climate, the current economic climate, a climate of fear. The pronunciation is /ˈklaɪmət/ – the last syllable is weak.

expressions.usage: pupil = a child at school (British English)
workforce = all the people who work for a company
behind = here: being the reason for
ulterior = kept secret because it is selfish; used almost only with "motive"
greed = a strong wish for more money or food than you need
inspire = fill somebody with the wish to do something

sentences.en: A good teacher knows how to motivate pupils.
sentences.az: Yaxşı müəllim şagirdləri necə həvəsləndirməyi bilir.

sentences.en: What was the motivation behind his decision?
sentences.az: Onun qərarının arxasında duran səbəb nə idi?

sentences.en: I think he had an ulterior motive for helping us.
sentences.az: Məncə, bizə kömək etməkdə onun gizli niyyəti var idi.

sentences.en: The crime was motivated by greed.
sentences.az: Cinayət tamahkarlıq zəminində törədilmişdi.

usage: To MOTIVATE somebody is to make them want to do something; a MOTIVE is the reason for an action, especially a crime; MOTIVATION is the desire to do something or the reason for it. "Highly motivated" is the standard description in job applications. The passive "be motivated BY" names the reason: motivated by money, by fear, by a desire to help. Pattern: motivate somebody TO do something.

expressions.usage: attitude TOWARDS / TO somebody or something
casual = not showing much care or thought
mature = behaving in a sensible, adult way
can-do = confident and willing to deal with problems
vary = be different from each other
reflect = show the nature of something

sentences.en: His attitude towards work has changed completely.
sentences.az: Onun işə münasibəti tamamilə dəyişib.

sentences.en: Attitudes to marriage vary from country to country.
sentences.az: Evliliyə münasibət ölkədən ölkəyə dəyişir.

sentences.en: She has a very mature attitude for her age.
sentences.az: Yaşına görə onun çox yetkin yanaşması var.

sentences.en: The film reflects the attitudes of the 1960s.
sentences.az: Film 1960-cı illərin baxışlarını əks etdirir.

usage: ATTITUDE is the way you think and feel about something, shown in your behaviour. The prepositions are TO and TOWARDS: "attitudes TO immigration". The basic adjectives are POSITIVE and NEGATIVE: "a positive attitude". In informal English, "an attitude problem" or simply "attitude" means unhelpful, rude behaviour. Do not confuse it with APTITUDE (natural ability).

lessons.azerbaijani: təsis etmək, qurmaq, yaratmaq; müəyyən etmək

expressions.usage: tie = a strong connection between people or countries
connection = something that links two things
reputation = the opinion people have of you
criteria = standards for judging; singular: criterion
firmly = in a strong, definite way
priority = something more important than other things

sentences.en: The company was established in 1995.
sentences.az: Şirkət 1995-ci ildə təsis edilib.

sentences.en: Police are trying to establish the identity of the victim.
sentences.az: Polis zərərçəkənin şəxsiyyətini müəyyən etməyə çalışır.

sentences.en: She quickly established a reputation as a reliable lawyer.
sentences.az: O, tezliklə etibarlı hüquqşünas kimi ad çıxardı.

sentences.en: The two countries established diplomatic ties in 1992.
sentences.az: İki ölkə 1992-ci ildə diplomatik əlaqələr qurdu.

usage: ESTABLISH has two main meanings: 1) start an organisation, system or relationship that is meant to last (establish a company, establish ties); 2) discover or prove the facts (establish the cause, establish that ...). It is more formal than "set up". "The Establishment" (with a capital letter) means the powerful people who control a country. WELL-ESTABLISHED describes something that has existed successfully for a long time.

lessons.azerbaijani: saxlamaq, qoruyub saxlamaq; texniki qulluq göstərmək; iddia etmək

expressions.usage: discipline = the practice of making people obey rules
dignity = calm behaviour that makes people respect you
status quo = the situation as it is now (Latin)
vehicle = a car, bus, lorry, etc.
maintain (that) + clause = keep saying that something is true
routine = done regularly as part of normal work
crew = a group of people working together

sentences.en: It is important to maintain a healthy weight.
sentences.az: Sağlam çəkini qoruyub saxlamaq vacibdir.

sentences.en: The teacher found it hard to maintain discipline.
sentences.az: Müəllim intizamı qorumaqda çətinlik çəkirdi.

sentences.en: He has always maintained that he is innocent.
sentences.az: O, həmişə günahsız olduğunu iddia edib.

sentences.en: The lift is closed for routine maintenance.
sentences.az: Lift planlı texniki qulluq üçün bağlıdır.

usage: MAINTAIN has three uses: 1) make something continue at the same level (maintain standards, maintain contact); 2) keep a machine, building or road in good condition; 3) formally, insist that something is true (maintain that ...). The noun is MAINTENANCE – notice the spelling change: maintAIN but maintENance, pronounced /ˈmeɪntənəns/. "Low-maintenance" describes something that needs little care.

expressions.usage: scandal = behaviour that shocks the public
plot = a secret plan to do something wrong
intention = what you plan to do
survey = a set of questions asked to many people
insight = a clear understanding of something
refuse = say that you will not do something

sentences.en: The report revealed serious flaws in the system.
sentences.az: Hesabat sistemdəki ciddi qüsurları üzə çıxardı.

sentences.en: A recent survey reveals that most people are worried about prices.
sentences.az: Son sorğu göstərir ki, insanların çoxu qiymətlərdən narahatdır.

sentences.en: The journalist refused to reveal her sources.
sentences.az: Jurnalist mənbələrini açıqlamaqdan imtina etdi.

sentences.en: The book contains shocking revelations about the royal family.
sentences.az: Kitabda kral ailəsi haqqında sarsıdıcı açıqlamalar var.

usage: REVEAL means to make known something that was secret or hidden. Patterns: reveal something TO somebody; reveal THAT + clause; reveal how / why / what. It is common in reporting research: "The study revealed that ...". A REVELATION is a surprising fact that is made known; "It was a revelation to me" means it changed how I understood something. REVEALING also describes clothes that show a lot of the body.

lessons.azerbaijani: (problemin) həllinə girişmək, mübarizə aparmaq; (idmanda) topu almağa cəhd etmək

expressions.usage: obesity = the condition of being extremely overweight
inequality = an unfair difference between groups of people
corruption = dishonest behaviour by people in power
discrimination = treating one group worse than others
shortage = a situation when there is not enough of something
congestion = roads being too full of traffic
opponent = the person you are playing against

expressions.az: problemlə birbaşa üzləşmək, qətiyyətlə həllinə girişmək
expressions.usage: head-on = in a direct and determined way

sentences.en: The government has promised to tackle corruption.
sentences.az: Hökumət korrupsiya ilə mübarizə aparmağa söz verib.

sentences.en: New measures are needed to tackle obesity among children.
sentences.az: Uşaqlar arasında piylənmə ilə mübarizə üçün yeni tədbirlər lazımdır.

sentences.en: The city built a new metro line to tackle congestion.
sentences.az: Şəhər tıxac problemini həll etmək üçün yeni metro xətti çəkdi.

sentences.en: It is better to tackle the problem head-on.
sentences.az: Problemlə birbaşa üzləşmək daha yaxşıdır.

usage: TACKLE means to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem. It takes a direct object, with no preposition: "tackle crime" – not "tackle with crime". It is a favourite verb in IELTS problem–solution essays, alongside ADDRESS, DEAL WITH and COMBAT. In football and rugby, to tackle a player is to try to take the ball from them. "Tackle somebody ABOUT something" means to speak to them directly about a difficult matter.

expressions.usage: electricity = the energy that makes machines and lights work
revenue = the money a company or government receives
wealth = a large amount of money and property
debate = a formal discussion or argument
enthusiasm = a strong feeling of interest and excitement
gap = a difference that separates people
young = having lived for only a short time
backup = extra equipment that you can use if the main one fails

sentences.en: Wind farms generate electricity without polluting the air.
sentences.az: Külək elektrik stansiyaları havanı çirkləndirmədən elektrik enerjisi istehsal edir.

sentences.en: Tourism generates a lot of revenue for the region.
sentences.az: Turizm regiona çoxlu gəlir gətirir.

sentences.en: The proposal has generated a great deal of debate.
sentences.az: Təklif geniş müzakirə doğurub.

sentences.en: The younger generation spends more time online than their parents.
sentences.az: Gənc nəsil valideynlərindən daha çox vaxtını internetdə keçirir.

usage: GENERATE means to produce or create something: energy (generate electricity, heat, power), money (generate income, profits, revenue), or reactions (generate interest, debate, excitement). The noun GENERATION most often means all the people born at about the same time: "the younger generation", "future generations", "for generations". A generation is also a period of about 25 to 30 years.

lessons.azerbaijani: təşviq etmək, təbliğ etmək; reklam etmək; vəzifəsini artırmaq

n.az: vəzifə artımı, həmçinin təbliğat və reklam kampaniyası

expressions.usage: cooperation = working together for a shared purpose
diversity = a range of different people or things
tolerance = willingness to accept different opinions
literacy = the ability to read and write

expressions.az: rifahı (sağlam və xoşbəxt yaşayışı) təşviq etmək

expressions.usage: actively = in a way that involves effort
deserve = have earned something by your actions

sentences.en: The organisation works to promote cooperation between universities.
sentences.az: Təşkilat universitetlər arasında əməkdaşlığı təşviq etmək üçün çalışır.

sentences.en: She was promoted to senior manager last year.
sentences.az: O, keçən il baş menecer vəzifəsinə yüksəldi.

sentences.en: Regular exercise promotes physical and mental well-being.
sentences.az: Müntəzəm idman fiziki və ruhi sağlamlığı möhkəmləndirir.

sentences.en: The job is interesting, but the promotion prospects are poor.
sentences.az: İş maraqlıdır, amma vəzifədə irəliləmə imkanları zəifdir.

usage: PROMOTE has three meanings: 1) help something to happen or develop (promote peace, promote health); 2) advertise a product (promote a new book); 3) move somebody to a higher job – usually passive: "be promoted TO manager". The noun PROMOTION covers all three: "get a promotion", "a sales promotion". In essays, PROMOTE is a precise alternative to "help" or "increase": promote awareness, promote understanding.

expressions.usage: freedom = the right to do or say what you want
import = a product brought in from another country

expressions.az: yalnız nə iləsə kifayətlənmək, özünü məhdudlaşdırmaq
expressions.usage: Reflexive pattern: I restrict myself to one coffee a day
impose = officially force a rule on people
lift = remove a rule or law
scope = the range of things that a subject covers
measure = an official action taken to deal with a problem

sentences.en: The new law restricts the sale of alcohol.
sentences.az: Yeni qanun spirtli içkilərin satışını məhdudlaşdırır.

sentences.en: Speed is restricted to 30 kilometres an hour in the town centre.
sentences.az: Şəhərin mərkəzində sürət saatda 30 kilometrlə məhdudlaşdırılıb.

sentences.en: The government imposed restrictions on foreign travel.
sentences.az: Hökumət xarici səfərlərə məhdudiyyətlər tətbiq etdi.

sentences.en: Most of the restrictions were lifted in the spring.
sentences.az: Məhdudiyyətlərin çoxu yazda götürüldü.

usage: RESTRICT means to limit the size, amount or range of something, usually by rules. Patterns: restrict something TO a limit ("restrict speed to 30 kilometres an hour"); restrict somebody FROM doing something; restrictions ON something. Compare LIMIT (neutral), RESTRICT (by rules or laws) and BAN (forbid completely). Verbs with RESTRICTIONS: impose / place, tighten, ease / relax, lift / remove.

n.az: uyğunlaşma, həmçinin ekranlaşdırma və ya səhnələşdirmə

expressions.usage: The basic pattern: adapt (yourself) TO something
circumstances = the conditions that affect a situation
survive = continue to live or exist
struggle = try very hard to do something difficult
accordingly = in a way that suits the situation
style = a particular way of doing something
species = a group of animals or plants of the same kind; plural: species

sentences.en: It took me a few months to adapt to the new job.
sentences.az: Yeni işə uyğunlaşmaq bir neçə ayımı aldı.

sentences.en: Some older workers struggle to adapt to new technology.
sentences.az: Bəzi yaşlı işçilər yeni texnologiyaya uyğunlaşmaqda çətinlik çəkirlər.

sentences.en: The novel was adapted for the screen in 2015.
sentences.az: Roman 2015-ci ildə ekranlaşdırılıb.

sentences.en: Good teachers adapt their style to the needs of the class.
sentences.az: Yaxşı müəllimlər üslublarını sinfin ehtiyaclarına uyğunlaşdırırlar.

usage: Three verbs are easily confused: ADAPT (change to suit new conditions), ADOPT (start to use a method, or take a child into your family) and ADJUST (make small changes). ADAPT is both intransitive (adapt TO a new life) and transitive (adapt a book FOR television). ADAPTABLE people cope well with change – a useful word in job applications. An ADAPTATION is also a film or play based on a book.

lessons.azerbaijani: töhfə vermək, pay vermək; səbəblərindən biri olmaq

expressions.az: nəyəsə töhfə vermək; nəyəsə səbəb olmaq

expressions.usage: generously = giving more than is usual
community = the people living in one area
spread = growth over a larger area
voluntary = done willingly, without being forced

sentences.en: Everyone contributed to the success of the project.
sentences.az: Layihənin uğuruna hər kəs töhfə verdi.

sentences.en: Stress can contribute to heart disease.
sentences.az: Stress ürək xəstəliyinə səbəb ola bilər.

sentences.en: She received an award for her outstanding contribution to science.
sentences.az: O, elmə verdiyi müstəsna töhfəyə görə mükafat aldı.

sentences.en: Poor hygiene contributed to the spread of the disease.
sentences.az: Gigiyenaya əməl olunmaması xəstəliyin yayılmasına səbəb oldu.

usage: CONTRIBUTE TO has two meanings: to give money, time or ideas to something shared, and to be one of the causes of something ("Smoking contributes to lung cancer"). The second meaning is very useful in cause–effect essays. After "contribute to" use a noun or -ing form, never an infinitive: "contribute to solving the problem". The usual verb with the noun is MAKE: "make a contribution TO".

lessons.azerbaijani: üzə çıxmaq, meydana çıxmaq, ortaya çıxmaq

expressions.usage: emerge AS + role: emerge as the favourite
shadow = a dark area where light is blocked
recession = a period when the economy is not growing
industry = the production of goods; a branch of business
power = here: a country with great influence
star = a famous and successful performer or player

sentences.en: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
sentences.az: Günəş buludların arxasından çıxdı.

sentences.en: It later emerged that the driver had fallen asleep.
sentences.az: Sonradan məlum oldu ki, sürücü yuxuya gedibmiş.

sentences.en: She has emerged as one of the country's leading writers.
sentences.az: O, ölkənin aparıcı yazıçılarından biri kimi önə çıxıb.

sentences.en: The economy is slowly emerging from recession.
sentences.az: İqtisadiyyat yavaş-yavaş tənəzzüldən çıxır.

usage: EMERGE means to come out of a place or a difficult situation, or to become known. It is intransitive – there is no passive ("was emerged" is wrong). Patterns: emerge FROM something; emerge AS something; it emerges THAT + clause. EMERGING is used before nouns for things that are beginning to develop: emerging markets, emerging technologies. Do not confuse EMERGENCE (appearing) with EMERGENCY (a dangerous situation).

expressions.az: izah etmək, səbəbi olmaq; (müəyyən hissəni) təşkil etmək
expressions.usage: Phrasal verb with two key meanings
bank = an organisation that keeps and lends money
eyewitness = a person who saw an event happen
deposit = money that you pay into a bank
vivid = producing very clear pictures in your mind
qualified = having passed the exams needed for a job

sentences.en: I'd like to open a bank account, please.
sentences.az: Zəhmət olmasa, bank hesabı açmaq istərdim.

sentences.en: The flight was delayed on account of bad weather.
sentences.az: Reys pis hava səbəbindən gecikdi.

sentences.en: Exports account for forty per cent of the country's income.
sentences.az: İxrac ölkə gəlirinin qırx faizini təşkil edir.

sentences.en: We must take the cost into account.
sentences.az: Biz xərci nəzərə almalıyıq.

usage: ACCOUNT has several important uses. 1) An arrangement with a bank: open / close an account. 2) A description of an event: "give an account of what happened". 3) ACCOUNT FOR = explain ("How do you account for the delay?") or form a part of a total ("Women account for 60 per cent of students") – essential for describing charts. Fixed phrases: TAKE something INTO ACCOUNT (nəzərə almaq), ON ACCOUNT OF (because of), ON NO ACCOUNT (under no circumstances).

expressions.usage: Very common linker: in terms of cost / quality
benefit = an advantage or useful effect
prison = a building where criminals are kept
uncertain = not sure; idiom = clearly and strongly
negotiate = reach an agreement by formal discussion
autumn = the season between summer and winter

sentences.en: In terms of price, the two phones are very similar.
sentences.az: Qiymət baxımından bu iki telefon çox oxşardır.

sentences.en: The long-term benefits of exercise are well known.
sentences.az: İdmanın uzunmüddətli faydaları hamıya məlumdur.

sentences.en: She told him in no uncertain terms that he was wrong.
sentences.az: O, haqsız olduğunu ona açıq-aşkar dedi.

sentences.en: "Carbon footprint" is a term used by environmentalists.
sentences.az: "Karbon izi" ekoloqların işlətdiyi termindir.

usage: TERM has four main meanings: 1) a word or phrase used as the name of something (a medical term); 2) a fixed period (a prison term, a term of office); 3) one of the periods of the British school year (the autumn term); 4) in the plural, the conditions of an agreement (terms and conditions). IN TERMS OF is one of the most useful phrases in academic English. "In the long term" and "in the short term" contrast future and immediate results; "come to terms with" means gradually accept something sad.

n.az: uzadılma, həmçinin əlavə tikili və daxili telefon nömrəsi

expressions.usage: Hedging phrase: I agree to some extent
The classic essay question: To what extent do you agree?
lesser = not as great as the other one
range = a variety of things of the same type
network = a system of connected lines, roads or people

sentences.en: To what extent do you agree with this statement?
sentences.az: Bu fikirlə nə dərəcədə razısınız?

sentences.en: I agree with you to a certain extent.
sentences.az: Mən səninlə müəyyən qədər razıyam.

sentences.en: She requested an extension of the deadline for her essay.
sentences.az: O, essenin təhvil verilmə müddətinin uzadılmasını xahiş etdi.

sentences.en: The city has an extensive network of cycle paths.
sentences.az: Şəhərdə geniş velosiped yolları şəbəkəsi var.

usage: EXTENT (noun, with "t") means how large or serious something is; EXTEND (verb, with "d") means to make longer or larger. "To some / a certain / a large extent" are hedging phrases that let you agree partly – very useful in discussion essays. "To what extent do you agree or disagree?" is the standard IELTS Task 2 question. EXTENSIVE means covering a large area or a lot of detail; do not confuse it with EXPENSIVE.
